messages:
Alex P: heads-up — noticing sustained queue depth growth on gpt-large-8q in us-west-2. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/queues?m=gpt-large-8q&r=us-west-2 :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Maya R: confirmed, per-model backlog is +1.3k reqs and increasing. GPU util on that pool is >93% and tail-latency slipping past 450ms.
SRE Bot: alert: queue_depth>1000 model=gpt-large-8q region=us-west-2 severity=warning
Jin T: any recent deploys? could be a model change that increased token generation time or batch sizing.
Maya R: no model deploys in last 6h. There was a large user job hitting that model from customer c-42 (batch scoring) starting ~1718602000.
Priya K: can we triage by routing new requests to eu-central-1 until we stabilize? Region capacity there is ~70% with spare GPUs.
Alex P: prefer admission control first to avoid global routing churn. lowering per-route concurrency for this model in us-west-2 should slow intake and let tail drain.
Leo G: agreed. proposing temporary policy: per-model max_concurrent=80 in us-west-2 and global qps cap 50 for gpt-large-8q. Apply for 15m then reassess.
Maya R: ok applying now.
Ops Runbook: executing admission change: redwoodctl adm-control set --model gpt-large-8q --region us-west-2 --max-concurrent 80 --qps 50 --reason "queue triage"
SRE Bot: admission_control_change: user=Priya K model=gpt-large-8q region=us-west-2 max_concurrent=80 qps=50 id=adm-7682
Jin T: monitoring backlog after change. current backlog 1320 -> 1100 and dropping. keep an eye on latency though.
Alex P: we should also shadow-route a small fraction to eu-central-1 for reliability if backlog stalls. command suggestion: redwoodctl route adjust --model gpt-large-8q --region us-west-2 --weight 0.9; --region eu-central-1 --weight 0.1
Priya K: can we throttle heavy API keys instead of global route? customer c-42 is the main offender. we can set key-level rate limits to reduce impact without affecting all users.
Maya R: customer-level throttle would be ideal. their key has been making large batch requests at 2x normal.
Leo G: added temporary key throttle: redwoodctl keys throttle --key c-42 --qps 10 --burst 20 --reason "protect cluster"
SRE Bot: key_throttle applied key=c-42 qps=10 id=throttle-221
Jin T: backlog down to 600 now, GPU util dropping to ~82%. tails improving.
Priya K: good. next steps: 1) keep admission limits for 30m, 2) contact c-42 CS to discuss best practices for batch scoring, 3) consider autoscale policy change for that pool.
Alex P: on autoscale — current policy has aggressive scale-up but conservative scale-down which means we might be slow to add nodes in sustained growth. we should evaluate quicker scale-up thresholds for peak windows.
Maya R: cost note: scaling up reserved capacity in us-west-2 will increase spend. Ops wants to avoid permanent change; prefer transient burst instances if possible.
Leo G: small action: enable ephemeral burst GPUs for that pool to add 3 nodes for 20m if queue depth > 800 for >5m. config snippet:
```
{
  "pool": "us-west-2-gpu-a",
  "burst_add": 3,
  "burst_ttl_mins": 20,
  "trigger": {"queue_depth_gte": 800, "duration_mins": 5}
}
```
Maya R: scheduling a quick postmortem if this repeats. capture root cause (customer behavior vs model perf) and add runbook steps.
Priya K: pinging customer success to flag c-42 (cc @CS).
Alex P: after backlog dips below 150 we'll lift the admission caps and remove throttles. leave burst nodes until traffic normalizes.
SRE Bot: queue_depth now 120, backlog draining. will auto-clear adm-change in 30m if metrics stable.
Ops Runbook: checklist for rollback:
- redwoodctl adm-control unset --id adm-7682
- redwoodctl keys unthrottle --id throttle-221
- redwoodctl route adjust --model gpt-large-8q --region us-west-2 --weight 1.0
Jin T: recording timeline for postmortem notes.
Maya R: thanks all. great incident play. :thumbsup:
Alex P: leaving monitoring on, will report back if it flares.
SRE Bot: thread closed by alert-suppression (auto) at 1718606025
